sections.Scope: Illustrative adult/adolescent asthma pathway; diagnosis, severity, comorbidities, and local guidance affect care.
sections.Assessment: Confirm variable respiratory symptoms and variable expiratory airflow when feasible; assess symptom control, exacerbation risk, inhaler technique, adherence, exposures, and comorbidities.
sections.Treatment: Use an inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing regimen. GINA's preferred Track 1 uses low-dose ICS-formoterol as needed for mild asthma and ICS-formoterol maintenance-and-reliever therapy (MART) for higher steps. Select step and dose from current control and risk; add-on LAMA or biologic assessment may be appropriate for selected uncontrolled severe asthma.
sections.Follow-up: Provide a written action plan; review control, exacerbations, adverse effects, inhaler technique, and adherence regularly; step treatment up or down only after reassessment.

sections.Scope: Illustrative stable adult COPD pathway; acute exacerbations require separate assessment.
sections.Assessment: Confirm persistent airflow obstruction by post-bronchodilator spirometry; assess symptoms, exacerbation history, exposure, oxygenation when indicated, and comorbidities.
sections.Treatment: Support smoking cessation and exposure reduction, vaccination, physical activity, and pulmonary rehabilitation when indicated. Use short-acting bronchodilator for relief; select long-acting bronchodilator therapy based on symptoms and exacerbation history, commonly LABA/LAMA. Consider ICS-containing triple therapy for selected patients with exacerbations and evidence suggesting benefit. Individualize oxygen and non-pharmacologic support.
sections.Follow-up: Reassess symptoms, exacerbations, inhaler technique, adherence, smoking, and adverse effects; investigate worsening or alternative causes.

sections.Scope: Illustrative adult type 2 diabetes pathway; not for type 1, gestational, or acute metabolic emergencies.
sections.Assessment: Confirm diagnosis and assess glycemia, cardiovascular and kidney disease, weight, hypoglycemia risk, complications, preferences, access, and treatment goals.
sections.Treatment: Provide individualized nutrition, activity, and diabetes self-management support. Select glucose-lowering therapy through shared decision-making. For established/high-risk ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD, prioritize agents with demonstrated relevant cardiovascular or kidney benefit regardless of baseline A1C when appropriate. Metformin remains an option for many patients; choose alternatives or combinations based on comorbidities, goals, risks, and preferences. Use insulin when clinically indicated.
sections.Follow-up: Monitor A1C or other appropriate glycemic measures, kidney function, cardiovascular risk, complications, medication effects, and goals; adjust therapy collaboratively.

sections.Scope: Illustrative adult CKD progression-risk pathway; specific cause and complications change management.
sections.Assessment: Establish chronicity and cause; classify by eGFR and albuminuria; review blood pressure, diabetes, cardiovascular risk, medications, and complications.
sections.Treatment: Address cause and cardiovascular risk, optimize blood pressure and glycemic care when relevant, and use renin-angiotensin system inhibition for appropriate albuminuric patients. Use an SGLT2 inhibitor for eligible CKD patients according to KDIGO criteria; consider other evidence-based kidney-protective therapy for selected patients. Adjust medication doses and avoid nephrotoxins where possible.
sections.Follow-up: Track eGFR and albuminuria, complications, potassium, medication tolerance, and progression risk; refer to nephrology when indicated and plan kidney replacement care for advanced disease.

condition: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)

sections.Scope: Illustrative chronic adult HFrEF pathway; acute decompensation and other ejection-fraction groups require tailored care.
sections.Assessment: Confirm heart failure and ejection fraction; identify cause, congestion, comorbidities, renal function, potassium, and functional status.
sections.Treatment: Relieve congestion with diuretics as needed. Initiate and titrate guideline-directed foundational therapy as tolerated: ARNI (or ACE inhibitor/ARB when appropriate), evidence-based beta-blocker, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor. Address cause, devices, rehabilitation, and advanced heart failure referral for selected patients.
sections.Follow-up: Monitor symptoms, volume status, blood pressure, renal function, potassium, and medication tolerance during titration; reinforce self-management and follow-up.

sections.Scope: Time-critical emergency pathway for suspected ACS; this record is an overview, not a substitute for emergency protocols.
sections.Initial response: Activate emergency evaluation. Obtain ECG promptly, assess stability, obtain serial cardiac troponin, and distinguish STEMI/NSTEMI/unstable angina while considering alternative emergencies.
sections.Treatment: Provide antithrombotic and anti-ischemic therapy as appropriate after contraindication assessment. Use urgent reperfusion, usually primary PCI, for eligible STEMI; select invasive strategy for NSTE-ACS according to risk. Begin secondary-prevention therapy and cardiac rehabilitation planning when appropriate.
sections.Follow-up: Monitor for ischemic and bleeding complications, assess ventricular function and risk, optimize secondary prevention, and arrange cardiac rehabilitation and follow-up.

sections.Scope: Illustrative outpatient migraine pathway; new red flags or sudden severe headache require urgent assessment.
sections.Assessment: Characterize headache pattern, associated symptoms, disability, medication use, triggers, and red flags; diagnose clinically and consider secondary causes when indicated.
sections.Acute treatment: Offer an individualized acute plan; options include an NSAID or paracetamol, and a triptan when appropriate. Consider an antiemetic. Avoid routine opioids and address medication-overuse risk.
sections.Prevention and follow-up: Discuss trigger management and preventive treatment when attacks or disability warrant it. Choose preventive therapy according to comorbidities, contraindications, and preferences; review response and adverse effects.

sections.Scope: Illustrative adult RA pathway; prompt specialist assessment is important when persistent inflammatory arthritis is suspected.
sections.Assessment: Confirm inflammatory arthritis and assess disease activity, function, prognostic factors, comorbidities, and baseline safety labs.
sections.Treatment: Use a treat-to-target approach with a conventional synthetic DMARD, commonly methotrexate when suitable, started promptly. Short-term glucocorticoids may be considered selectively while DMARD effect begins, balancing harms. If target is not reached, adjust or combine DMARDs; biologic or targeted synthetic DMARDs may be used after individualized risk review.
sections.Follow-up: Measure disease activity and function regularly, adjust therapy toward remission or low disease activity, monitor toxicity and infection risk, and maintain vaccination and cardiovascular risk care.

sections.Scope: Illustrative care overview; cognitive impairment has multiple causes and requires diagnostic evaluation.
sections.Assessment: Evaluate history, function, cognition, medications, mood, sensory factors, and potentially reversible contributors; establish diagnosis and stage with appropriate testing.
sections.Treatment: Provide person-centered care, safety planning, caregiver support, and management of behavioral and medical needs. Cholinesterase inhibitors or memantine may be considered according to stage and patient factors. Anti-amyloid therapy may be considered only for eligible early-stage patients after confirmatory evaluation and shared decision-making about benefits, risks, monitoring, and access.
sections.Follow-up: Review cognition, function, safety, caregiver needs, medication benefit and harms, and advance care planning over time.

sections.Scope: Illustrative adult Parkinson disease pathway; atypical parkinsonism requires specialist assessment.
sections.Assessment: Assess motor and non-motor symptoms, function, falls, cognition, mood, sleep, and medication effects; involve a movement-disorder specialist when available.
sections.Treatment: Offer levodopa when motor symptoms affect quality of life. For less disabling symptoms, choose among levodopa, dopamine agonist, or MAO-B inhibitor based on individual risks and preferences. Encourage exercise and consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and management of non-motor symptoms.
sections.Follow-up: Review motor response, wearing-off, dyskinesia, impulse-control and other adverse effects, falls, swallowing, cognition, and caregiver needs; adjust therapy with specialist input.
